title: Goodbye, Things: The New Japanese Minimalism
author: Fumio Sasaki
target_audience: Adults interested in minimalism and decluttering
People seeking lifestyle changes for more simplicity or contentment
Fans of Japanese culture and philosophies
Anyone exploring the psychological impact of ownership
core_themes: Minimalism as a path to happiness and clarity
Letting go of attachment to material possessions
primary_purpose: To illustrate the transformative power of minimalist living by sharing the author’s personal journey, practical tips, and philosophical insights, encouraging readers to let go of excess possessions and discover happiness, focus, and authenticity in a less cluttered life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, personal, and candid with reflective anecdotes
structure_format.organization: Divided into short, titled chapters covering insights, practical decluttering advice, lists of benefits, and the author's before-and-after experiences
features: Reflections on the psychological effects of minimalism
References to other minimalists and Japanese culture

key_concepts_lessons: Owning fewer things frees mental space and encourages personal growth.
Attachment to objects often stems from fear, insecurity, or habit.
Minimalism is not deprivation but choosing what truly matters.
Decluttering is a step-by-step process best approached incrementally.
True value and happiness are found in relationships and experiences, not possessions.
Letting go creates room for gratitude, self-discovery, and authentic living.
notable_features: Relatable, everyday perspective of an ordinary person (not an expert)
Illustrated with before-and-after photos of the author's living space
Contrasts Western materialism with Japanese minimalism
cultural_historical_context: Part of a larger minimalist movement in Japan influenced by space-conscious living and zen philosophy; the book gained international popularity in the late 2010s amid growing global interest in minimalism, mindfulness, and the KonMari method.
reception_impact: International bestseller with high praise for its simplicity and relatability
Helped expand the minimalist movement beyond Japan
Praised for demystifying and humanizing minimalism
Critics sometimes note the advice may overemphasize purging for its own sake or may not address complex family/household decluttering scenarios
comparable_titles: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up by Marie Kondo
Essentialism: The Disciplined Pursuit of Less by Greg McKeown
Minimalism: Live a Meaningful Life by Joshua Fields Millburn & Ryan Nicodemus
